title: Legacy generation_params overwrites model and messages after model allow-list validation

evidence.behavior: A synthetic JSON provider with allowed_models=[permitted-model] and generation_params.model=disallowed-model is accepted by the real loader. Registry.defaultParams feeds it to the real generator, which emits disallowed-model and replacement messages after validating permitted-model. No live request.

impact: The effective model/prompt can differ from the fields the adapter validates. The legacy narrative route consumes these defaultParams; the personal-provider loader separately protects bound fields, so that path is not claimed vulnerable. The configuration must be operator-authored/altered; no unprivileged remote exploit is claimed.
requirement_source: User continuation stages 1,2: configuration must reach actual consumers and hidden precedence must be explicit.
CLAUDE.md rule 4: No silent unit, provider or method substitution.
R42 data/configuration test: policy is in merge order despite existence of JSON.
interpretation: Unvalidated arbitrary parameter spreading defeats an explicitly configured allow-list. This is a precedence defect, not a reason to remove provider profiles.

title: A valid palette profile creates an invalid new figure because defaultFigure hardcodes accessible

evidence.behavior: Rename palette ids in a synthetic profile and recompute its valid contentHash. validateWorkbenchProfile accepts; defaultFigure still assigns accessible; real WorkbenchService.profileForFigure rejects this generated figure.

impact: Moving available palettes into JSON does not make the new-figure default follow the profile. A valid supported custom palette registry produces unusable default state until another consumer manually corrects it. No claim that all custom profiles fail.
requirement_source: User continuation stage1: detect policy hidden in helpers/read order after JSON extraction.
R42: user/domain display choices are data; a different palette does not change the renderer algorithm.
CLAUDE.md rule3: export defaults and UI labels live in versioned validated hashed configuration.
interpretation: Default identity is hardcoded despite configurable palette registry; the failing real consumer confirms more than a literal search.
